real_life_application.question: In a Geogebra sketch of M = [[1, 3], [2, 6]], the row space R(M) appears as a line whose slope equals which value?
real_life_application.explanation: R(M) is spanned by (1, 3), giving the line y = 3x with slope 3; the other lines (C, N) have different slopes.

real_life_application.question: When plotting M = [[1, 3], [2, 6]], the column space C(M) should be drawn as a line through which origin in ℝ²?
real_life_application.explanation: Every column space passes through the origin because M·0 = 0, so C(M) is a line through the shared origin.

real_life_application.question: In a 2D Geogebra plot of M = [[1, 3], [2, 6]], the null space N(M) should be visually verified as perpendicular to which subspace?
real_life_application.explanation: The fundamental theorem gives R(M) ⊥ N(M), so N(M) should be drawn perpendicular to the row line through origin.

real_life_application.question: For a rank-1 2x2 matrix, the four fundamental subspaces reduce to how many distinct lines in ℝ²?
real_life_application.explanation: R(M) and N(M) are perpendicular lines, and C(M) and N(Mᵀ) are another perpendicular pair; in 2D, R(M) ≠ C(M) generally, yielding three or four distinct lines.

real_life_application.question: A data analyst uses M = [[1, 3], [2, 6]] to model two perfectly collinear feature vectors; the rank-deficient geometry reveals which real-world interpretation?
real_life_application.explanation: Rank 1 (rows are multiples) means the two features carry one piece of information; the second is linearly redundant.

real_life_application.question: In signal processing, a noisy signal is decomposed into a component in C(A) plus a component in N(Aᵀ); the noise component lies in which subspace?
real_life_application.explanation: Noise modeled as unobservable lives in N(Aᵀ), the left null space, which is orthogonal to the signal subspace C(A).

real_life_application.question: In a least-squares regression, the residual vector r = b − A·x̂ is constrained to live in which fundamental subspace?
real_life_application.explanation: The normal equations force Aᵀ·r = 0, so the residual lies in N(Aᵀ), perpendicular to the model column space C(A).

real_life_application.question: A Green's function for a boundary-value PDE relates the kernel of a differential operator to which companion subspace?
real_life_application.explanation: The Green's function solves the PDE by inverting on the range, mapping the kernel complement to the range of the operator.

real_life_application.question: In quantum mechanics, eigenspaces of a Hermitian operator for distinct eigenvalues are always which of the following?
real_life_application.explanation: Hermitian operators have orthogonal eigenspaces; this is a direct physical realization of the R(A) ⊥ N(A) pairing.

real_life_application.question: For a 3x3 matrix of rank 2, the dimension of its null space in ℝ³ must be which value?
real_life_application.explanation: By rank-nullity, nullity = 3 − rank = 3 − 2 = 1, so N(A) is a 1D line through the origin complementary to the 2D row space.

topics.title: Null space of M and of Mᵀ

real_life_application.question: For a rank-1 design matrix X in statistics, the right null space N(X) corresponds to which geometric object in the parameter space?
real_life_application.explanation: N(X) is the set of parameter directions that produce zero fitted values; one such direction identifies one linear constraint.

real_life_application.question: The left null space N(Xᵀ) of a design matrix gives which economically meaningful vector in regression diagnostics?
real_life_application.explanation: Projectors onto N(Xᵀ) reveal data points that the model cannot fit; their norms are the leverage scores.

real_life_application.question: A symmetric matrix A has the special property that N(A) equals which other subspace?
real_life_application.explanation: Symmetry gives A = Aᵀ, so the right and left null spaces coincide; this identifies invariant directions of A.

real_life_application.question: For a non-symmetric rank-1 matrix, N(A) and N(Aᵀ) generally turn out to be which kind of subspaces?
real_life_application.explanation: When A ≠ Aᵀ, the right and left null spaces differ: for M = [[1,3],[2,6]], N(M) has slope −1/3 and N(Mᵀ) has slope −1/2.

real_life_application.question: The right null space N(A) and the left null space N(Aᵀ) always share which scalar quantity?
real_life_application.explanation: Both have dimension n − rank(A) (or m − rank(A)); this shared nullity is the dimension count from rank-nullity.

real_life_application.question: To verify the four-subspaces theorem on a 3x3 rank-2 matrix, one confirms by inner product that C(M) is perpendicular to which subspace?
real_life_application.explanation: The fundamental theorem pairs C(M) with N(Mᵀ) as orthogonal complements in ℝᵐ; checking ⟨c, n⟩ = 0 verifies it.

real_life_application.question: In a 4x4 matrix of rank 3, the dimension of the left null space N(Mᵀ) is forced to be which value?
real_life_application.explanation: dim(N(Mᵀ)) = m − rank = 4 − 3 = 1; one direction in ℝ⁴ lies orthogonal to every column of M.

real_life_application.question: The projection onto C(M) along N(Mᵀ) is well-defined because C(M) and N(Mᵀ) together satisfy which property?
real_life_application.explanation: Because C(M) ⊥ N(Mᵀ) and their dimensions sum to m, every vector in ℝᵐ splits uniquely into a C(M) plus N(Mᵀ) part.

real_life_application.question: In a coding-theory view, the orthogonal complement relationship between C(M) and N(Mᵀ) is exactly the same as which dual notion?
real_life_application.explanation: C(M) plays the role of a code and N(Mᵀ) the role of its dual parity-check space; the pairing R ⊥ N is the same orthogonality.

real_life_application.question: For the 3x3 matrix A = [[1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6], [7, 8, 9]], the dimension of R(A) is which value?
real_life_application.explanation: This special matrix has rank 2, so the row space is a 2D plane in ℝ³, paired with the 1D null space (1, −2, 1).

real_life_application.question: For A = [[1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6], [7, 8, 9]], the vector (1, −2, 1) is the kernel direction; applied to a linear map, it acts as which kind of invariant?
real_life_application.explanation: Being in N(A) means A·(1, −2, 1) = 0; this is a direction along which the linear map collapses everything to zero.

real_life_application.question: Applying the SVD to A = [[1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6], [7, 8, 9]] yields how many nonzero singular values?
real_life_application.explanation: Rank 2 implies exactly two nonzero singular values; the third column of U and V is the kernel direction (1, −2, 1).

real_life_application.question: In a numerical linear algebra computation, the four subspaces of A = [[1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6], [7, 8, 9]] reveal that the matrix behaves like which simpler object?
real_life_application.explanation: Although A is 3x3, every output lies in a 2D plane; the rank-2 reduction is what compresses the data.

real_life_application.question: A data scientist fits A = [[1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6], [7, 8, 9]] and finds exact linear dependence in the columns; the column space C(A) is which geometric object?
real_life_application.explanation: C(A) is the 2D plane spanned by (1, 4, 7) and (2, 5, 8); the third column adds no new direction.

real_life_application.question: For the matrix A = [[1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6], [7, 8, 9]], the kernel vector (1, −2, 1) can be interpreted physically as which failure mode of the map?
real_life_application.explanation: Any input along (1, −2, 1) is destroyed by A; this direction is the one piece of information the map cannot recover.

topics.title: 4x4 matrix M with range of various dimensions

real_life_application.question: A 4x4 graphics transformation that preserves all four dimensions is best modeled by which canonical matrix?
real_life_application.explanation: Identity (or any invertible matrix) has rank 4, so its range is all of ℝ⁴ — no dimension is lost.

real_life_application.question: A 4x4 stereo projection that flattens 3D world points onto a 2D screen is a map whose range has which dimension?
real_life_application.explanation: Projection onto a 2D plane collapses two dimensions; the output subspace is 2D, so rank 2.

real_life_application.question: A rank-1 4x4 transformation collapses its 4D input onto which kind of geometric object?
real_life_application.explanation: Rank 1 means the range is 1D, so all 4D inputs are squashed onto one line through the origin.

real_life_application.question: When a 4x4 transform has rank 3, the null space of the map has which dimension?
real_life_application.explanation: Rank-nullity for 4x4 gives nullity = 4 − rank = 4 − 3 = 1; one direction in the input is lost.

real_life_application.question: A 4x4 zero matrix used in a layered neural network layer represents a map whose range is which kind of set?
real_life_application.explanation: The zero map sends every input to 0, so its range is the 0D set {0}; effectively the layer transmits nothing.

topics.title: Range of A contains S, T

real_life_application.question: In quantum mechanics, the range of an observable equals the set of which physically meaningful numbers?
real_life_application.explanation: The spectrum of a Hermitian operator equals the set of possible measurement outcomes — real scalars in the range.

real_life_application.question: In control theory, the reachable set of a linear time-invariant system is the range of which constructed matrix?
real_life_application.explanation: The controllability matrix [B, AB, A²B, …] has its column space exactly equal to the reachable set of states.

real_life_application.question: A linear signal-processing system A has output space equal to the range of A; because A is linear, this output space is always which kind of set?
real_life_application.explanation: Linearity forces the image to be closed under linear combinations, so the output space is itself a subspace.

real_life_application.question: In computer graphics, a perspective projection sends 3D world points onto a 2D image plane; this image plane is a 2D subspace inside which surrounding space?
real_life_application.explanation: The 2D rendered image sits inside the 3D screen coordinate frame as a 2D subspace; nearer pixels are still 3D observations.

real_life_application.question: An economist constructs a linear model A mapping policy inputs to predicted outcomes; the set of achievable outcomes is the range of A, which is always which type of object?
real_life_application.explanation: Because A is linear, its achievable set is closed under linear combinations — a linear subspace, not a curved region.
